one_liner: WooCommerce is a free, open-source WordPress plugin whose REST API (wc/v3) is authenticated with merchant-generated consumer key/secret, so a builder can self-host a store and test right away.
auth_notes: Merchant generates a Consumer Key/Secret in WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API. Over HTTPS the key is the Basic Auth username and the secret is the password. Over HTTP, OAuth 1.0a HMAC-SHA1 signing is used, which is why OTHER is listed. WordPress Application Passwords are used for the MCP/abilities path. There is no OAuth2 flow for the core REST API.
access_notes: No developer programme or application is needed. WooCommerce is a free plugin, so a developer can run a store on their own WordPress site and generate keys. Each customer's store is self-hosted, so a store URL has to be collected per user.
blocker_notes: Each user must supply their own store URL and generate keys. HTTPS and pretty permalinks are required. These are per-customer setup steps, not blockers for the builder.

evidence.quote: Pre-generated keys can be used to authenticate use of the REST API endpoints.
Over HTTPS, send the Consumer Key as the Basic Auth username and the Consumer Secret as the password
WooCommerce implements OAuth 1.0a signing with HMAC-SHA1 and no token exchange step
There is no developer programme and nothing to apply for.
This allows WC data to be created, read, updated, and deleted using requests in JSON format and using WordPress REST API Authentication methods and standard HTTP verbs
WooCommerce registers product and order abilities in WordPress. With the MCP Adapter plugin, AI clients can discover and run these store operations through the Model Context Protocol
